item.content:encoded:
I believe it is because in the case of a breach of containment - which could concern more than one instance - any mammal still asleep or unconscious could become infected, thus risking a major outbreak, while the population can be easily brought back to before breach numbers in a month at most.

That doesn't seem crazy to me to include termination in the containment protocols of a skip that's duplicable without significant costs.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I know this is an old entry, but why do the containment protocols call for the destruction of the thing? Shouldn't this be fairly easy to contain as long as there's nobody asleep? You could even leave one D-class asleep to lure it in and then dispose of the offspring when it reproduces.

item.title: I find the special containment procedures lacking
item.content:encoded:
If it can't move across sand and salt is harmful to it; why not keep it's container on top of and surrounded by sand covering a radius longer than it can jump, and then around that sand, salt; require that there is always that much sand and salt around any path where it is expected to be moved, and similar requirements for anyone infected. Also have all the outside doors and windows of the facility protected by a laminar flow of brine mist, require all water piped into the facility to come pre-salted (with desalinization done only inside the facility), and all sewers to be mixed with brine before being allowed out, and any outgoing living things with organs as well as any outgoing containers to be run thru a MRI scan to verify there are no stowaways?

Oh, and of course, have it's container sit on top of a wireless solar powered scale, rigged to sound an alarm if the power goes off or if the container becomes lighter, with a spotlight outside of the salt radius hooked to a UPS, aimed at the scale's solar panel.

Sure, containment breaches are reasonably difficult to track but it's not like it'd be hard to find if it started reproducing. Just look for the dude whose chest exploded.
